key_insight: A data-driven generalized Navier-Stokes model learns non-equilibrium stress and heat-flux corrections from Boltzmann data to extend fluid modeling into the transition regime beyond continuum validity.
engineering_relevance: This offers a lower-cost surrogate for kinetic simulation that could improve predictive accuracy in rarefied-gas and microfluidic flow applications where standard Navier-Stokes breaks down.
method: Learns a mapping from equilibrium states, density, velocity, temperature, and Knudsen number to non-equilibrium variables.
Uses end-to-end training on numerical Boltzmann-equation data to fit the generalized closure.
Introduces long-term end-to-end learning to reduce error accumulation in time-dependent predictions.
evidence_signal: The model is validated on multiple benchmark cases, including 1D wave and Riemann problems and 2D isentropic vortex and Taylor-Green vortex problems.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of Boltzmann-generated training data, so extrapolation to unseen regimes may be limited.
paper_title: Learning a generalized Navier-Stokes model beyond the continuum regime
